source_text: Pridie quoque cum illam caenam ultimam, quam liberam uocant, quantum in ipsis erat non caenam liberam sed agapen caenarent, eadem constantia ad populum uerba iactabant, comminantes iudicium dei, contestantes passionis suae felicitatem, inridentes concurrentium curiositatem, dicente Saturo: Crastinus uobis satis non est, quod libenter uidetis quos odistis? Hodie amici, cras inimici? Notate tamen uobis facies nostras diligenter, ut recognoscatis nos in die illo. Ita omnes inde adtoniti discedebant: ex quibus multi crediderunt.
thought_title: Bold Speech at the Last Dinner
orientation: The redactor narrates the prisoners last meal on the day before they are led into the arena.
pass_a_gloss: Also on the day before, when they were eating that last dinner, which they call free, as far as it lay in them eating it not as a free dinner but as a love meal, with the same firmness they kept hurling words at the people, threatening the judgment of God, calling to witness the blessedness of their martyrdom, mocking the curiosity of those running together, with Saturus saying: Is tomorrow not enough for you, that you gladly look at those whom you hate? Today friends, tomorrow enemies? Nevertheless mark our faces for yourselves carefully, so that you may recognize us on that day. Thus all astonished were leaving from there: from these many believed.

choices.why: Brief fixes passio as martyrdom, so felicitatem must stay a general blessed state, not Felicity or suffering.
Keeps Roman free dinner label distinct from Christian agape meal without importing Eucharist.
Literal genitive threat spoken to the crowd, not a last judgment system term.
Literal demonstrative kept vague as in Latin, without fixing it to Judgment Day.

pass_b_english: On the day before too, when they sat down to that last dinner they call the free dinner, they ate it, as far as they were able, not as a free dinner but as a love meal. With the same constancy they hurled words at the crowd. They warned of the judgment of God, called them to witness the blessedness of their martyrdom, and mocked the curiosity of those who had rushed together to stare.

Saturus said, "Is tomorrow not enough for you, that you gladly look at those you hate? Friends today, enemies tomorrow? But mark our faces carefully for yourselves, so that you may recognize us on that day." So they all left that place stunned, and many of them believed.
